microtheory.name: rhythm_meter
microtheory.definition: Temporal organization of music — beat, tempo, meter, polyrhythm, syncopation, groove, microtiming. The dimension of musical structure orthogonal to pitch. Substrate analogue: temporal pattern grammar applied to substrate's onset event stream.

concepts.name: pulse
concepts.definition: Underlying regular tick implied by music. Listeners + performers extract a common pulse. Substrate analogue: substrate's periodicity-extractor output.

concepts.name: tactus
concepts.definition: Most natural pulse rate, ~600ms (100bpm). Foot-tap speed. Lerdahl + Jackendoff. Substrate analogue: substrate's preferred clock rate.

concepts.name: subdivision
concepts.definition: Faster pulse subdividing beat — eighths, sixteenths, triplets. Substrate analogue: substrate's finer-grain temporal grid.

concepts.name: beat_classes
concepts.definition: Within a measure: 1 = strong; 3 = medium; 2 + 4 = weak (in 4/4). Substrate analogue: substrate's per-position-in-cycle weighting.

concepts.name: time_signature
concepts.definition: Notation: 4/4 means 4 quarter-note beats per measure. 3/4, 6/8, 5/4, 7/8. Substrate analogue: substrate's measure-structure parameter.

concepts.name: simple_meter
concepts.definition: Each beat divides into 2. 2/4, 3/4, 4/4. Substrate analogue: substrate's binary subdivision tracker.

concepts.name: compound_meter
concepts.definition: Each beat divides into 3. 6/8, 9/8, 12/8. Substrate analogue: substrate's ternary subdivision tracker.

concepts.name: irregular_meter
concepts.definition: 5/4, 7/8, 11/16. Groups of 2 + 3 alternating. Bartók, Dave Brubeck. Substrate analogue: substrate's non-uniform period tracker.

concepts.name: polymeter
concepts.definition: Two or more meters simultaneously. 3 against 4. Substrate analogue: substrate's parallel periodicity tracking.

concepts.name: polyrhythm
concepts.definition: Two or more conflicting rhythmic patterns simultaneously. 3:2 (hemiola) is classic. African + Latin music. Substrate analogue: substrate's multi-stream rhythm parsing.

concepts.name: hemiola
concepts.definition: Specific 3:2 polyrhythm — two beats of three against three beats of two. Substrate analogue: substrate's locked 3:2 period detection.

concepts.name: cross_rhythm
concepts.definition: Sustained polyrhythm felt as conflict. Substrate analogue: substrate's parallel-conflicting-period state.

concepts.name: syncopation
concepts.definition: Accent on weak beat or off-beat. Creates tension; expected metric position is silenced or weak. Substrate analogue: substrate's metric-expectation-violation.

concepts.name: swing
concepts.definition: Long-short subdivision feel. Eighth note pairs played as ~2:1 instead of 1:1. Jazz fundamental. Substrate analogue: substrate's non-isochronous subdivision template.

concepts.name: shuffle
concepts.definition: Triplet-based subdivision feel. Blues + shuffle rhythms. Substrate analogue: substrate's ternary subdivision template.

concepts.name: groove
concepts.definition: The sustained urge-to-move quality. Janata 2012. Depends on subtle timing relationships. Substrate analogue: substrate's high-coherence rhythmic state driving motor reflex.

concepts.name: microtiming
concepts.definition: Sub-beat deviations from grid. Drummer pushing or laying back. Critical for feel. Substrate analogue: substrate's beat-tracking with phase-deviation tolerance.

concepts.name: anacrusis
concepts.definition: Pickup notes leading into the downbeat. Phrase begins before measure 1. Substrate analogue: substrate's leading-up-to-attractor phrase shape.

concepts.name: phrase_rhythm
concepts.definition: Hierarchical grouping above the bar. 2-bar, 4-bar, 8-bar phrases. Substrate analogue: substrate's nested temporal grouping.

concepts.name: rubato
concepts.definition: Expressive tempo variation — speeding up + slowing down for emphasis. Romantic-era + jazz. Substrate analogue: substrate's tempo-tracker with rapid-adaptation mode.

concepts.name: tempo_range
concepts.definition: Larghissimo (<20bpm) → Prestissimo (>200bpm). Natural perception ~80-160 bpm. Substrate analogue: substrate's clock-rate range.

concepts.name: metronome_marking
concepts.definition: Notation: ♩= 120 means quarter note = 120 bpm. Substrate analogue: substrate's beat-rate parameter.

concepts.name: accelerando_ritardando
concepts.definition: Gradual speeding up + slowing down. Italian musical terms. Substrate analogue: substrate's tempo-trajectory parameter.

rules.name: tactus_is_substrates_preferred_pulse_rate
rules.head: the substrate is presented with a wide tempo range
rules.body: it most readily extracts a pulse near ~120bpm (tactus); extremes degrade beat tracking. Substrate's natural clock-rate.

rules.name: subdivision_supports_microtiming
rules.head: the substrate tracks beats with sub-beat precision
rules.body: the subdivision grid (2 or 3 per beat) lets microtiming deviations be measured + felt. Substrate's grid-based temporal precision.

rules.name: syncopation_creates_tension_via_expectation_violation
rules.head: the substrate expects an accent on a strong beat
rules.body: an accent on a weak beat + silence on the strong beat creates tension. Resolution restores metric alignment. Substrate's metric expectation.

rules.name: swing_alters_subdivision_template
rules.head: the substrate is in a swing context
rules.body: eighth-note pairs are perceived + produced as long-short (~2:1) rather than even. Per-style subdivision template. Substrate's contextual rhythm prior.

rules.name: polyrhythm_requires_parallel_period_tracking
rules.head: the substrate hears two rhythms at conflicting periods (3:2)
rules.body: it tracks both periods in parallel; tension comes from mismatched alignment. Substrate's multi-stream periodicity.
